revenue_by_merchant.sql:
SELECT m.merchant_name,
       SUM(t.amount) as total_revenue,
       COUNT(*) as txn_count
FROM fact_transactions t, dim_merchant m
WHERE t.merchant_id = m.merchant_id
AND t.transaction_date > '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY m.merchant_name
ORDER BY total_revenue
LIMIT 10;

issues.title: Incorrect revenue calculation
issues.problem: Revenue should only include transactions with status 'COMPLETED', but all transactions are included.
issues.fix: SUM(CASE WHEN t.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) as total_revenue

issues.title: Potential performance issue with implicit join
issues.problem: Using implicit join syntax can lead to less readable and potentially slower queries.
issues.fix: FROM fact_transactions t JOIN dim_merchant m ON t.merchant_id = m.merchant_id

issues.title: Lack of comments on complex logic
issues.problem: The logic for calculating total revenue is not commented on, making it harder to understand.
issues.fix: /* Revenue is calculated by summing the amount for completed transactions only */

review.corrected_sql: SELECT m.merchant_name, SUM(CASE WHEN t.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) as total_revenue, COUNT(*) as txn_count FROM fact_transactions t JOIN dim_merchant m ON t.merchant_id = m.merchant_id WHERE t.transaction_date > '2024-01-01' GROUP BY m.merchant_name ORDER BY total_revenue LIMIT 10;
review.summary: The query has a critical correctness issue with revenue calculation and a readability issue with lack of comments. It also uses an implicit join which can be replaced with an explicit join for better readability and maintainability.

customer_spend.sql:
SELECT c.customer_name, c.email, c.tier,
       SUM(t.amount) as lifetime_value,
       COUNT(t.transaction_id) as total_orders
FROM dim_customer c
LEFT JOIN fact_transactions t ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id
WHERE t.status = 'COMPLETED'
GROUP BY c.customer_name, c.email
HAVING SUM(t.amount) > 1000
ORDER BY lifetime_value DESC;

issues.title: Missing Revenue Calculation
issues.problem: The query does not calculate revenue as per the business rule.
issues.fix: Add a SUM(amount) WHERE status = 'COMPLETED' calculation for revenue.

issues.title: Incorrect Group By Clause
issues.problem: Grouping by email and customer_name can lead to incorrect aggregations if customers have the same name.

issues.title: Lack of Comments
issues.problem: The query lacks comments explaining the logic and calculations.
issues.fix: Add comments to explain the purpose of each calculation and join.

issues.title: Inconsistent Naming
issues.problem: The alias 'c' for dim_customer and 't' for fact_transactions are not descriptive enough.
issues.fix: Use more descriptive aliases like 'cust' for dim_customer and 'trans' for fact_transactions.

review.corrected_sql:
SELECT cust.customer_name, cust.email, cust.tier,
       SUM(CASE WHEN trans.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN trans.amount ELSE 0 END) as revenue,
       SUM(trans.amount) as lifetime_value,
       COUNT(trans.transaction_id) as total_orders
FROM dim_customer cust
LEFT JOIN fact_transactions trans ON cust.customer_id = trans.customer_id
GROUP BY cust.customer_id, cust.customer_name, cust.email, cust.tier
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN trans.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN trans.amount ELSE 0 END) > 1000
ORDER BY revenue DESC;
review.summary: The query has critical correctness issues and readability concerns. It needs to correctly calculate revenue and should include comments for better understanding.

daily_failure_rate.sql:
SELECT transaction_date,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_transactions f2
        WHERE f2.status = 'FAILED'
        AND f2.transaction_date = t.transaction_date) as failed_count,
       COUNT(*) as total_count,
       failed_count / total_count * 100 as failure_rate
FROM fact_transactions t
GROUP BY transaction_date
ORDER BY transaction_date;

issues.title: Incorrect calculation of failure rate
issues.problem: The failure rate is calculated incorrectly because failed_count is not defined in the SELECT clause but used in the calculation.
issues.fix: Use a subquery or a window function to calculate the failure rate correctly.

issues.title: Correlated subquery
issues.line: (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_transactions f2 WHERE f2.status = 'FAILED' AND f2.transaction_date = t.transaction_date) as failed_count
issues.problem: The correlated subquery can be inefficient as it runs for each row in the outer query.
issues.fix: Use a JOIN or a window function to calculate the failed_count.

issues.title: Lack of comments
issues.problem: The query lacks comments explaining the logic and calculations.
issues.fix: Add comments to explain the purpose of each part of the query.

review.corrected_sql: WITH daily_transactions AS (SELECT transaction_date, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'COMPLETED') AS completed_count, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'FAILED') AS failed_count FROM fact_transactions GROUP BY transaction_date) SELECT transaction_date, failed_count, completed_count + failed_count AS total_count, (failed_count * 100.0 / (completed_count + failed_count)) AS failure_rate FROM daily_transactions ORDER BY transaction_date;
review.summary: The query had issues with the calculation of failure rate, performance due to a correlated subquery, and readability due to lack of comments. The corrected query uses a CTE for better readability and performance.
